AI NEWS DAILY — 10 Nov 2026

TOP STORY
Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on one base with different guardrails: Fable 5.2 is open to all, Mythos 5.2 goes only to vetted researchers. The headline is price, not benchmarks — $8 per million input and $40 per million output tokens, about 20% cheaper than the 5.1 generation.

5 KEY UPDATES
1. Meta shipped Muse Ember at $0.10 per million input tokens, built as the cheap execution layer for agents: tool calls, routing, extraction, long document parsing, 1M-token context.
2. OpenAI agreed to acquire Astral, the team behind uv, Ruff and ty, and will fold it into Codex while keeping the open-source projects supported.
3. Anthropic's amended filing reports $17B in Q3 revenue against roughly $895B in compute and infrastructure commitments. Separately, it committed about $3.4B for 1.7GW of gas-fired generators.
4. OpenAI and Anthropic both claim algorithms bearing on the 25-year-old Exponential Time Hypothesis; Anthropic lists Claude as an author and includes a Lean 4 formal proof. An independent review is being organised.
5. Open weights: Baidu published ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base as a 280B MoE pre-training checkpoint, and Meituan shipped LongCat-2.5, a 1.6T multimodal model for long-horizon agentic coding.

CONCEPT OF THE DAY — The Price of a Thought
Three labs launched models in one day and each led with money, not benchmarks. The buyer changed: an agent calls a model hundreds of times per task, so cost per completed task, not cost per token, decides whether a deployment survives its budget review. Research is attacking the same problem — CPU-ARC compiles a reasoning trace into a CPU-executable cache 16 to 291 times cheaper to invoke, and Energy-Based Reasoners stop looping when the state is good enough, reaching 99.9% on Sudoku-Extreme with 345 times less compute.
